test: fix FluxIT login race condition causing CI timeouts (#4300)

The helloAdmin test was timing out in CI because the login() method had a race condition between form submission and page navigation. The test would click the login form submit button (triggering a POST to /login) and immediately call open() to navigate to /flux, causing the navigation to race with the form POST redirect.

Fixed by adding proper waits after form submission:
- waitForDocumentReady() to ensure form POST completes
- waitUntil() to ensure Spring Security redirect completes before navigating

This matches the pattern used in the working SecurityIT test.

* fix: handle null loadingCount in grid test waitForLoading method

The waitForLoading method in AbstractGridTest was causing NullPointerException
when globalThis.Vaadin.connectionState.loadingCount was undefined or null.
This occurred when the Vaadin object or connectionState wasn't initialized yet
during test execution.

Changes:
- Add optional chaining (?.) in JavaScript to safely access nested properties
- Use nullish coalescing (?? 0) to default to 0 when value is undefined/null
- Check if result is a Number instance before calling intValue() in Java

Fixes all 12 failing tests in ReadOnlyGridWithHeaderFilterIT,
GridUseDataProviderHookIT, ReadOnlyGridCustomFilterIT, ReadOnlyGridOrFilterIT,
and ReadOnlyGridSinglePropertyFilterIT that were failing with the same
NullPointerException at AbstractGridTest.java:124.

fix: stop replacing vaadinBuildFrontend task to preserve Flow configuration (#4746)

The Hilla Gradle plugin called tasks.replace("vaadinBuildFrontend",
EngineBuildFrontendTask::class.java), which created a new task instance
that lost configuration applied by in the `vaadin` section of the build
file (for example filterClasspath).

EngineBuildFrontendTask was an empty class adding no behavior over
VaadinBuildFrontendTask. Remove the task replacement and delete the
unused class.

Fixes #4745

Add --ignore-scripts to npm ci in setup action (#5062) (CP: 25.1) (#5076)

Add --ignore-scripts to npm ci in setup action (#5062)

Prevents npm postinstall scripts from executing during dependency
installation in CI workflows. This mitigates supply chain attacks
like the recent axios compromise (GHSA-fw8c-xr5c-95f9) where a
malicious postinstall script in a transitive dependency executed
arbitrary code on the runner.

Dependencies are installed from package-lock.json (npm ci), so
postinstall scripts are not needed for correct resolution. Build
steps that require compiled native modules should run npm rebuild
explicitly.

Add --ignore-scripts to npm ci in setup action (#5062)

Prevents npm postinstall scripts from executing during dependency
installation in CI workflows. This mitigates supply chain attacks
like the recent axios compromise (GHSA-fw8c-xr5c-95f9) where a
malicious postinstall script in a transitive dependency executed
arbitrary code on the runner.

Dependencies are installed from package-lock.json (npm ci), so
postinstall scripts are not needed for correct resolution. Build
steps that require compiled native modules should run npm rebuild
explicitly.

chore: update package[-lock].json (25.2) (#5892)

* chore: update package[-lock].json

* fix: do not trigger the production frontend build from hillaGenerate

Flow 25.3 registers the production frontend bundle as an extra output
directory of the main source set (vaadin/flow#25024), which makes the
`classes` lifecycle task depend on `vaadinBuildFrontend`. Since
hillaGenerate depended on `classes`, running it started a full production
frontend build first: the bundle got built before the endpoints were
generated, and the frontend files Flow generates for the bundle -
node_modules included - were cleaned up afterwards, so the generator could
no longer resolve @vaadin/hilla-generator-cli and the task failed with

    GeneratorException: Unable to resolve npm package "@vaadin/hilla-generator-cli"

Depend on the source set compile tasks and processResources instead of the
`classes` lifecycle task, and add a functional test asserting that
hillaGenerate keeps the compile tasks but does not pull in
vaadinBuildFrontend.

Add --ignore-scripts to npm ci in setup action (#5062) (CP: 25.1) (#5076)

Add --ignore-scripts to npm ci in setup action (#5062)

Prevents npm postinstall scripts from executing during dependency
installation in CI workflows. This mitigates supply chain attacks
like the recent axios compromise (GHSA-fw8c-xr5c-95f9) where a
malicious postinstall script in a transitive dependency executed
arbitrary code on the runner.

Dependencies are installed from package-lock.json (npm ci), so
postinstall scripts are not needed for correct resolution. Build
steps that require compiled native modules should run npm rebuild
explicitly.

test: fix FluxIT login race condition causing CI timeouts (#4300) (CP: 24.9) (#4304)

test: fix FluxIT login race condition causing CI timeouts (#4300)

The helloAdmin test was timing out in CI because the login() method had a race condition between form submission and page navigation. The test would click the login form submit button (triggering a POST to /login) and immediately call open() to navigate to /flux, causing the navigation to race with the form POST redirect.

Fixed by adding proper waits after form submission:
- waitForDocumentReady() to ensure form POST completes
- waitUntil() to ensure Spring Security redirect completes before navigating

This matches the pattern used in the working SecurityIT test.

Add --ignore-scripts to npm ci in setup action (#5062) (CP: 24.10) (#5075)

Add --ignore-scripts to npm ci in setup action (#5062)

Prevents npm postinstall scripts from executing during dependency
installation in CI workflows. This mitigates supply chain attacks
like the recent axios compromise (GHSA-fw8c-xr5c-95f9) where a
malicious postinstall script in a transitive dependency executed
arbitrary code on the runner.

Dependencies are installed from package-lock.json (npm ci), so
postinstall scripts are not needed for correct resolution. Build
steps that require compiled native modules should run npm rebuild
explicitly.

fix: enforce version consistency in Gradle tests (#4074)

- Remove hardcoded versions from Gradle test configurations
- Read all versions (Hilla, Flow, Spring Boot) from root pom.xml
- Fail tests immediately if versions cannot be determined
- Pass versions as system properties to Gradle plugin tests
- No fallback values allowed - ensures version consistency

This prevents version drift between Maven-defined versions and
Gradle test configurations, particularly important for Spring Boot
milestone releases.

fix: generate valid OpenAPI for bare generic types (#4238)

Problem:
When Java endpoints use raw generic types like:
  public List getBareList() { return null; }

The parser generated invalid OpenAPI missing the required 'items' field:
  {"type": "array", "nullable": true}

According to OpenAPI 3 spec, ArraySchema.items is a required field, but
the generated schema omitted it entirely.

Solution:
Always initialize ArraySchema with items set to anySchema() (ObjectSchema)
in SchemaProcessor. This ensures valid OpenAPI is generated upfront. If
TypeSignaturePlugin later discovers type arguments, it will override the
items field with the specific type. If no type arguments are found (bare
generics), the default ObjectSchema remains, generating valid OpenAPI.

test: fix FluxIT login race condition causing CI timeouts (#4300)

The helloAdmin test was timing out in CI because the login() method had a race condition between form submission and page navigation. The test would click the login form submit button (triggering a POST to /login) and immediately call open() to navigate to /flux, causing the navigation to race with the form POST redirect.

Fixed by adding proper waits after form submission:
- waitForDocumentReady() to ensure form POST completes
- waitUntil() to ensure Spring Security redirect completes before navigating

This matches the pattern used in the working SecurityIT test.

fix: Use environment protection for pull_request_target workflows

After GitHub's December 2025 changes to pull_request_target:
- Workflows now always run from default branch (not PR branch)

See: https://bybowu.com/article/dec-8-fix-github-actions-pull-request-target-now

Because TB tests require secrets, we need pull_request_target to run
validations on forked branches. The pr-tests environment ensures only
authorized reviewers can approve workflow runs from forks.

Changes:
- validation.yml: Use pull_request_target with environment protection
- skip-validation.yml: Add branches filter to pull_request_target
- Fix concurrency group syntax bug
- Use _ prefix for private environment variables

test: add full-stack testing infrastructure for Java → TypeScript generation (#4297)

* feat: add full-stack testing infrastructure for Java → TypeScript

Phase 1 of consolidating generator tests to verify complete Java → TypeScript
pipeline instead of split Java→OpenAPI and OpenAPI→TypeScript tests.

New infrastructure components:

1. **NodeRunner.java** - Utility for executing Node.js scripts from Java tests
   - Captures stdout/stderr
   - Handles timeouts
   - Throws exceptions on non-zero exit codes

2. **run-generator.mjs** - Node.js script that runs TypeScript generator
   - Reads OpenAPI JSON from stdin

* fix: work around Rolldown cross-chunk binding bug in ITs

Rolldown (used by Vite 8) has a bug where minified identifier names
in a dynamic-import chunk collide with cross-chunk runtime bindings,
causing "TypeError: t is not a function" at runtime. This affects the
markdown-helpers chunk created by @vaadin/tooltip's lazy import of
@vaadin/markdown/src/markdown-helpers.js.

Force the markdown-helpers module into the main chunk via manualChunks
to avoid the broken cross-chunk binding entirely.

Add --ignore-scripts to npm ci in setup action (#5062)

Prevents npm postinstall scripts from executing during dependency
installation in CI workflows. This mitigates supply chain attacks
like the recent axios compromise (GHSA-fw8c-xr5c-95f9) where a
malicious postinstall script in a transitive dependency executed
arbitrary code on the runner.

Dependencies are installed from package-lock.json (npm ci), so
postinstall scripts are not needed for correct resolution. Build
steps that require compiled native modules should run npm rebuild
explicitly.

chore: Make project TypeScript 6 compatible (#5209)

* fix: make custom sw.ts TS 6 compatible

Flow was upgraded to TypeScript 6, which no longer provides a global
'process' type by default. Replace 'process.env.NODE_ENV === development'
with 'import.meta.env.DEV' to match Flow's canonical sw.ts.

* fix: remove unnecessary InputEvent cast for TS 6

TS 6 infers the NumberField onInput handler parameter as InputEvent,
so the explicit 'as InputEvent' cast is flagged as unnecessary by the
no-unnecessary-type-assertion ESLint rule.

chore: update package[-lock].json (25.2) (#5892)

* chore: update package[-lock].json

* fix: do not trigger the production frontend build from hillaGenerate

Flow 25.3 registers the production frontend bundle as an extra output
directory of the main source set (vaadin/flow#25024), which makes the
`classes` lifecycle task depend on `vaadinBuildFrontend`. Since
hillaGenerate depended on `classes`, running it started a full production
frontend build first: the bundle got built before the endpoints were
generated, and the frontend files Flow generates for the bundle -
node_modules included - were cleaned up afterwards, so the generator could
no longer resolve @vaadin/hilla-generator-cli and the task failed with

    GeneratorException: Unable to resolve npm package "@vaadin/hilla-generator-cli"

Depend on the source set compile tasks and processResources instead of the
`classes` lifecycle task, and add a functional test asserting that
hillaGenerate keeps the compile tasks but does not pull in
vaadinBuildFrontend.

test: wait for the Kotlin Gradle application to answer before testing (#6004)

bootStart launched the application and then slept for ten seconds, which
is not enough on a slower machine: the Windows run had it still setting
up JPA when the integration tests connected, so all three of them failed
with "Could not connect to http://localhost:8888" and the application was
killed before it ever finished starting.

Poll the application until it serves a request instead, giving up after
two minutes. A build that starts too slowly now says so, and one whose
application dies during startup reports the exit code rather than a
connection error from every test.

failed four tests on the Windows runner.

Cache the unpacked distribution instead, keyed on the file that pins the
version.

fix: keep React Fast Refresh working for views with a config export (#5576) (CP: 25.2) (#6033)

fix: keep React Fast Refresh working for views with a config export (#5576)

* fix: keep React Fast Refresh working for views with a config export

@vitejs/plugin-react v6 adds its refresh footer in a plugin that runs
after the file-router's pre-enforced transform, so the previous regex
injection into that footer never matched and editing a view with a
static `config: ViewConfig` export caused a full page reload instead of
HMR.

Replace the injection with the refresh runtime's
`window.__getReactRefreshIgnoredExports` hook: each view file registers
its module id so the `config` export is skipped during refresh boundary
validation. Config changes still propagate through the regenerated
file-routes.ts module.

Fixes #5159

* refactor: deliver the React Refresh ignore hook via a virtual module

Incorporates the improvements from #5316:

- Install window.__getReactRefreshIgnoredExports once through a virtual
  module imported by every view file, instead of duplicating the
  installer in each transformed view. View files keep registering their
  exact module ids, so private (_-prefixed) and non-route files under
  the views directory retain stock Fast Refresh semantics.
- Skip the production-mode name preservation for anonymous default
  exports, where the regex captured the function/class keyword and
  produced invalid code, and support named default class exports.
- Test the installed hook behavior (scoping, chaining with a
  pre-existing hook) in a vm context, and cover the production-mode
  transform.

test: fix FluxIT login race condition causing CI timeouts (#4300) (CP: 24.9) (#4304)

test: fix FluxIT login race condition causing CI timeouts (#4300)

The helloAdmin test was timing out in CI because the login() method had a race condition between form submission and page navigation. The test would click the login form submit button (triggering a POST to /login) and immediately call open() to navigate to /flux, causing the navigation to race with the form POST redirect.

Fixed by adding proper waits after form submission:
- waitForDocumentReady() to ensure form POST completes
- waitUntil() to ensure Spring Security redirect completes before navigating

This matches the pattern used in the working SecurityIT test.

Add --ignore-scripts to npm ci in setup action (#5062) (CP: 24.10) (#5075)

Add --ignore-scripts to npm ci in setup action (#5062)

Prevents npm postinstall scripts from executing during dependency
installation in CI workflows. This mitigates supply chain attacks
like the recent axios compromise (GHSA-fw8c-xr5c-95f9) where a
malicious postinstall script in a transitive dependency executed
arbitrary code on the runner.

Dependencies are installed from package-lock.json (npm ci), so
postinstall scripts are not needed for correct resolution. Build
steps that require compiled native modules should run npm rebuild
explicitly.

chore: bump dompurify to 3.4.11 to match the Vaadin bundles 24.10.5 peer dependency (#6139)

* chore: align dompurify with the @vaadin/bundles 24.10.5 peer dependency

The prepare script syncs the web component versions from vaadin/platform
24.10, which now resolves to 24.10.5. @vaadin/bundles 24.10.5 declares an
optional peer dependency on dompurify 3.4.11 while the root package.json
still pinned 3.4.8, so npm install died with an ERESOLVE conflict (which
npm reports without any message) and every build on the branch failed
before running a single test.

Bump dompurify to 3.4.11, commit the web component version updates that
the prepare script generates anyway, and regenerate the lock file.

* .

* chore: bump react-router to 7.18.3 to match Flow 24.10 (#6145)

Flow 24.10 raised the react-router version it injects into applications
from 7.18.2 to 7.18.3 in vaadin/flow#25393, while Hilla still pinned
7.18.2. The Kotlin Gradle test application ends up with both: Flow writes
7.18.3 into the application package.json, but the Hilla packages linked
into it with file: references resolve react-router from the repository
root, where 7.18.2 was hoisted.

Two react-router instances in the same bundle means the router created by
one of them is invisible to the other, so useViewConfig() -- which calls
useMatches() -- fails with "useMatches must be used within a data router"
and the application renders an error page instead of the view. All three
Kotlin Gradle integration tests then time out waiting for their first
element. The Maven test applications are unaffected because they are npm
workspaces of this repository and share the single hoisted copy.

Align the pinned version with Flow so that a single react-router is
resolved again, and regenerate the lock file.

test: wait for the Kotlin Gradle application to answer before testing (#6004) (CP: 24.10) (#6007)

test: wait for the Kotlin Gradle application to answer before testing (#6004)

bootStart launched the application and then slept for ten seconds, which
is not enough on a slower machine: the Windows run had it still setting
up JPA when the integration tests connected, so all three of them failed
with "Could not connect to http://localhost:8888" and the application was
killed before it ever finished starting.

Poll the application until it serves a request instead, giving up after
two minutes. A build that starts too slowly now says so, and one whose
application dies during startup reports the exit code rather than a
connection error from every test.

Co-authored-by: Artur Signell <artur@vaadin.com>

test: retry the TestKit Gradle distribution download in gradle-plugin tests (#6014) (CP: 24.10) (#6018)

* test: retry the TestKit Gradle distribution download in gradle-plugin tests (#6014)

The functional tests run the build under test with a pinned Gradle version,
which TestKit downloads from services.gradle.org. A network hiccup during
that download fails the test before the build even starts, which took out
four tests on the Windows runner with "Could not install Gradle distribution
from ... Unexpected end of file from server".

Retry the build up to three times when it fails while installing or
connecting to the distribution. Failures of the build under test are
rethrown as before.

* test: make the TestKit Gradle version a TestProject property

The distribution-download retry logs the Gradle version being downloaded,
but on this branch the version was hardcoded inside createGradleRunner, so
the reference did not compile. Expose it as a constructor property, as on
main.

Add --ignore-scripts to npm ci in setup action (#5062) (CP: 24.9) (#5078)

Add --ignore-scripts to npm ci in setup action (#5062)

Prevents npm postinstall scripts from executing during dependency
installation in CI workflows. This mitigates supply chain attacks
like the recent axios compromise (GHSA-fw8c-xr5c-95f9) where a
malicious postinstall script in a transitive dependency executed
arbitrary code on the runner.

Dependencies are installed from package-lock.json (npm ci), so
postinstall scripts are not needed for correct resolution. Build
steps that require compiled native modules should run npm rebuild
explicitly.

test: wait for the Kotlin Gradle application to answer before testing (#6004) (CP: 24.9) (#6009)

test: wait for the Kotlin Gradle application to answer before testing (#6004)

bootStart launched the application and then slept for ten seconds, which
is not enough on a slower machine: the Windows run had it still setting
up JPA when the integration tests connected, so all three of them failed
with "Could not connect to http://localhost:8888" and the application was
killed before it ever finished starting.

Poll the application until it serves a request instead, giving up after
two minutes. A build that starts too slowly now says so, and one whose
application dies during startup reports the exit code rather than a
connection error from every test.

test: retry the TestKit Gradle distribution download in gradle-plugin tests (#6014) (CP: 24.9) (#6020)

* test: retry the TestKit Gradle distribution download in gradle-plugin tests (#6014)

The functional tests run the build under test with a pinned Gradle version,
which TestKit downloads from services.gradle.org. A network hiccup during
that download fails the test before the build even starts, which took out
four tests on the Windows runner with "Could not install Gradle distribution
from ... Unexpected end of file from server".

Retry the build up to three times when it fails while installing or
connecting to the distribution. Failures of the build under test are
rethrown as before.

* test: make the TestKit Gradle version a TestProject property

The distribution-download retry logs the Gradle version being downloaded,
but on this branch the version was hardcoded inside createGradleRunner, so
the reference did not compile. Expose it as a constructor property, as on
main.

fix: generate valid OpenAPI for bare generic types (#4238)

Problem:
When Java endpoints use raw generic types like:
  public List getBareList() { return null; }

The parser generated invalid OpenAPI missing the required 'items' field:
  {"type": "array", "nullable": true}

According to OpenAPI 3 spec, ArraySchema.items is a required field, but
the generated schema omitted it entirely.

Solution:
Always initialize ArraySchema with items set to anySchema() (ObjectSchema)
in SchemaProcessor. This ensures valid OpenAPI is generated upfront. If
TypeSignaturePlugin later discovers type arguments, it will override the
items field with the specific type. If no type arguments are found (bare
generics), the default ObjectSchema remains, generating valid OpenAPI.

test: fix FluxIT login race condition causing CI timeouts (#4300)

The helloAdmin test was timing out in CI because the login() method had a race condition between form submission and page navigation. The test would click the login form submit button (triggering a POST to /login) and immediately call open() to navigate to /flux, causing the navigation to race with the form POST redirect.

Fixed by adding proper waits after form submission:
- waitForDocumentReady() to ensure form POST completes
- waitUntil() to ensure Spring Security redirect completes before navigating

This matches the pattern used in the working SecurityIT test.

unused class.

Add --ignore-scripts to npm ci in setup action (#5062)

Prevents npm postinstall scripts from executing during dependency
installation in CI workflows. This mitigates supply chain attacks
like the recent axios compromise (GHSA-fw8c-xr5c-95f9) where a
malicious postinstall script in a transitive dependency executed
arbitrary code on the runner.

Dependencies are installed from package-lock.json (npm ci), so
postinstall scripts are not needed for correct resolution. Build
steps that require compiled native modules should run npm rebuild
explicitly.

* fix: make custom sw.ts TS 6 compatible

Flow was upgraded to TypeScript 6, which no longer provides a global
'process' type by default. Replace 'process.env.NODE_ENV === development'
with 'import.meta.env.DEV' to match Flow's canonical sw.ts.

* fix: remove unnecessary InputEvent cast for TS 6

TS 6 infers the NumberField onInput handler parameter as InputEvent,
so the explicit 'as InputEvent' cast is flagged as unnecessary by the
no-unnecessary-type-assertion ESLint rule.

chore: update package[-lock].json (25.2) (#5892)

* chore: update package[-lock].json

* fix: do not trigger the production frontend build from hillaGenerate

Flow 25.3 registers the production frontend bundle as an extra output
directory of the main source set (vaadin/flow#25024), which makes the
`classes` lifecycle task depend on `vaadinBuildFrontend`. Since
hillaGenerate depended on `classes`, running it started a full production
frontend build first: the bundle got built before the endpoints were
generated, and the frontend files Flow generates for the bundle -
node_modules included - were cleaned up afterwards, so the generator could
no longer resolve @vaadin/hilla-generator-cli and the task failed with

    GeneratorException: Unable to resolve npm package "@vaadin/hilla-generator-cli"

Depend on the source set compile tasks and processResources instead of the
`classes` lifecycle task, and add a functional test asserting that
hillaGenerate keeps the compile tasks but does not pull in
vaadinBuildFrontend.

test: wait for the Kotlin Gradle application to answer before testing (#6004)

bootStart launched the application and then slept for ten seconds, which
is not enough on a slower machine: the Windows run had it still setting
up JPA when the integration tests connected, so all three of them failed
with "Could not connect to http://localhost:8888" and the application was
killed before it ever finished starting.

Poll the application until it serves a request instead, giving up after
two minutes. A build that starts too slowly now says so, and one whose
application dies during startup reports the exit code rather than a
connection error from every test.

fix: keep React Fast Refresh working for views with a config export (#5576) (CP: 25.2) (#6033)

fix: keep React Fast Refresh working for views with a config export (#5576)

* fix: keep React Fast Refresh working for views with a config export

@vitejs/plugin-react v6 adds its refresh footer in a plugin that runs
after the file-router's pre-enforced transform, so the previous regex
injection into that footer never matched and editing a view with a
static `config: ViewConfig` export caused a full page reload instead of
HMR.

Replace the injection with the refresh runtime's
`window.__getReactRefreshIgnoredExports` hook: each view file registers
its module id so the `config` export is skipped during refresh boundary
validation. Config changes still propagate through the regenerated
file-routes.ts module.

Fixes #5159

* refactor: deliver the React Refresh ignore hook via a virtual module

Incorporates the improvements from #5316:

- Install window.__getReactRefreshIgnoredExports once through a virtual
  module imported by every view file, instead of duplicating the
  installer in each transformed view. View files keep registering their
  exact module ids, so private (_-prefixed) and non-route files under
  the views directory retain stock Fast Refresh semantics.
- Skip the production-mode name preservation for anonymous default
  exports, where the regex captured the function/class keyword and
  produced invalid code, and support named default class exports.
- Test the installed hook behavior (scoping, chaining with a
  pre-existing hook) in a vm context, and cover the production-mode
  transform.

test: wait for the grid rows before using them in react-crud tests (#6259)

## Summary
The `GridController` test helper handed out a grid before it had
rendered any rows, so react-crud tests failed randomly on slow CI
machines. The helper now really waits for the rows and gives a clear
error when a row is missing.

## What changed
`packages/ts/react-crud/test/GridController.ts`:

- `init()` checks now throw instead of returning a falsy value.
`waitFor` only retries when the callback throws, so the old checks
passed on the first try and returned a grid with no rows.
- `init()` also waits until `grid.loading` is `false`, because the data
provider loads items asynchronously.
- New `waitForBodyRow(row)` waits until the requested physical row
exists.
- `toggleRowSelected(row)` waits for the row before clicking it.
- `getBodyCell(row, col)` throws a named error when the row is not
rendered, instead of the confusing `Cannot read properties of undefined
(reading 'querySelectorAll')`.

## Test summary
This branch changes a shared test helper only; it adds no new test
methods.

| # | Status | What the test verifies | Why it matters |
|---|--------|------------------------|----------------|
| 1 | ✅ | Tests that call `GridController.init()` and then read rows or
toggle selection (the existing react-crud grid, AutoGrid and AutoCrud
suites) now run against a grid that has finished loading | This was the
actual flake: without the wait, row lookups returned `undefined` on slow
machines |
| 2 | ❗ **gap** | `waitForBodyRow` / `getBodyCell` throw a descriptive
error when a row never renders | If this regressed, real failures would
again show up as an unrelated `querySelectorAll` error and be hard to
debug |

- No test method was added or changed. Row 1 is covered indirectly by
every existing react-crud test that uses `GridController`.

Deliberately untested: the helper's own error messages (row 2). They
only improve failure output, and adding a test for a test helper's error
text was not judged worth the extra fixture.

Add --ignore-scripts to npm ci in setup action (#5062) (CP: 25.1) (#5076)

Add --ignore-scripts to npm ci in setup action (#5062)

Prevents npm postinstall scripts from executing during dependency
installation in CI workflows. This mitigates supply chain attacks
like the recent axios compromise (GHSA-fw8c-xr5c-95f9) where a
malicious postinstall script in a transitive dependency executed
arbitrary code on the runner.

Dependencies are installed from package-lock.json (npm ci), so
postinstall scripts are not needed for correct resolution. Build
steps that require compiled native modules should run npm rebuild
explicitly.

test: wait for the Kotlin Gradle application to answer before testing (#6004) (CP: 25.1) (#6008)

test: wait for the Kotlin Gradle application to answer before testing (#6004)

bootStart launched the application and then slept for ten seconds, which
is not enough on a slower machine: the Windows run had it still setting
up JPA when the integration tests connected, so all three of them failed
with "Could not connect to http://localhost:8888" and the application was
killed before it ever finished starting.

Poll the application until it serves a request instead, giving up after
two minutes. A build that starts too slowly now says so, and one whose
application dies during startup reports the exit code rather than a
connection error from every test.

test: retry the TestKit Gradle distribution download in gradle-plugin tests (#6014) (CP: 25.1) (#6019)

test: retry the TestKit Gradle distribution download in gradle-plugin tests (#6014)

The functional tests run the build under test with a pinned Gradle version,
which TestKit downloads from services.gradle.org. A network hiccup during
that download fails the test before the build even starts, which took out
four tests on the Windows runner with "Could not install Gradle distribution
from ... Unexpected end of file from server".

Retry the build up to three times when it fails while installing or
connecting to the distribution. Failures of the build under test are
rethrown as before.

test: fix FluxIT login race condition causing CI timeouts (#4300) (CP: 24.9) (#4304)

test: fix FluxIT login race condition causing CI timeouts (#4300)

The helloAdmin test was timing out in CI because the login() method had a race condition between form submission and page navigation. The test would click the login form submit button (triggering a POST to /login) and immediately call open() to navigate to /flux, causing the navigation to race with the form POST redirect.

Fixed by adding proper waits after form submission:
- waitForDocumentReady() to ensure form POST completes
- waitUntil() to ensure Spring Security redirect completes before navigating

This matches the pattern used in the working SecurityIT test.

Add --ignore-scripts to npm ci in setup action (#5062) (CP: 24.9) (#5078)

Add --ignore-scripts to npm ci in setup action (#5062)

Prevents npm postinstall scripts from executing during dependency
installation in CI workflows. This mitigates supply chain attacks
like the recent axios compromise (GHSA-fw8c-xr5c-95f9) where a
malicious postinstall script in a transitive dependency executed
arbitrary code on the runner.

Dependencies are installed from package-lock.json (npm ci), so
postinstall scripts are not needed for correct resolution. Build
steps that require compiled native modules should run npm rebuild
explicitly.

test: wait for the Kotlin Gradle application to answer before testing (#6004) (CP: 24.9) (#6009)

test: wait for the Kotlin Gradle application to answer before testing (#6004)

bootStart launched the application and then slept for ten seconds, which
is not enough on a slower machine: the Windows run had it still setting
up JPA when the integration tests connected, so all three of them failed
with "Could not connect to http://localhost:8888" and the application was
killed before it ever finished starting.

Poll the application until it serves a request instead, giving up after
two minutes. A build that starts too slowly now says so, and one whose
application dies during startup reports the exit code rather than a
connection error from every test.

test: retry the TestKit Gradle distribution download in gradle-plugin tests (#6014) (CP: 24.9) (#6020)

* test: retry the TestKit Gradle distribution download in gradle-plugin tests (#6014)

The functional tests run the build under test with a pinned Gradle version,
which TestKit downloads from services.gradle.org. A network hiccup during
that download fails the test before the build even starts, which took out
four tests on the Windows runner with "Could not install Gradle distribution
from ... Unexpected end of file from server".

Retry the build up to three times when it fails while installing or
connecting to the distribution. Failures of the build under test are
rethrown as before.

* test: make the TestKit Gradle version a TestProject property

The distribution-download retry logs the Gradle version being downloaded,
but on this branch the version was hardcoded inside createGradleRunner, so
the reference did not compile. Expose it as a constructor property, as on
main.

- Read all versions (Hilla, Flow, Spring Boot) from root pom.xml
- Fail tests immediately if versions cannot be determined
- Pass versions as system properties to Gradle plugin tests

Gradle test configurations, particularly important for Spring Boot
milestone releases.

fix: generate valid OpenAPI for bare generic types (#4238)

Problem:
When Java endpoints use raw generic types like:
  public List getBareList() { return null; }

The parser generated invalid OpenAPI missing the required 'items' field:
  {"type": "array", "nullable": true}

According to OpenAPI 3 spec, ArraySchema.items is a required field, but
the generated schema omitted it entirely.

Solution:
Always initialize ArraySchema with items set to anySchema() (ObjectSchema)
in SchemaProcessor. This ensures valid OpenAPI is generated upfront. If
TypeSignaturePlugin later discovers type arguments, it will override the
items field with the specific type. If no type arguments are found (bare
generics), the default ObjectSchema remains, generating valid OpenAPI.

test: fix FluxIT login race condition causing CI timeouts (#4300)

The helloAdmin test was timing out in CI because the login() method had a race condition between form submission and page navigation. The test would click the login form submit button (triggering a POST to /login) and immediately call open() to navigate to /flux, causing the navigation to race with the form POST redirect.

Fixed by adding proper waits after form submission:
- waitForDocumentReady() to ensure form POST completes
- waitUntil() to ensure Spring Security redirect completes before navigating

This matches the pattern used in the working SecurityIT test.

Because TB tests require secrets, we need pull_request_target to run
validations on forked branches. The pr-tests environment ensures only
authorized reviewers can approve workflow runs from forks.

Changes:
- validation.yml: Use pull_request_target with environment protection
- skip-validation.yml: Add branches filter to pull_request_target
- Fix concurrency group syntax bug
- Use _ prefix for private environment variables

test: add full-stack testing infrastructure for Java → TypeScript generation (#4297)

* feat: add full-stack testing infrastructure for Java → TypeScript

Phase 1 of consolidating generator tests to verify complete Java → TypeScript
pipeline instead of split Java→OpenAPI and OpenAPI→TypeScript tests.

New infrastructure components:

1. **NodeRunner.java** - Utility for executing Node.js scripts from Java tests
   - Captures stdout/stderr
   - Handles timeouts
   - Throws exceptions on non-zero exit codes

2. **run-generator.mjs** - Node.js script that runs TypeScript generator
   - Reads OpenAPI JSON from stdin
   - Imports all generator plugins dynamically
   - Outputs generated files as JSON to stdout

3. **FullStackTestHelper.java** - Main test helper class
   - Executes full pipeline: Java → OpenAPI → TypeScript
   - Parses generator output
   - Provides assertions against snapshot files

4. **TypeScriptComparator.java** - File comparison utility
   - Line-by-line diff with clear error messages
   - Whitespace normalization

Add --ignore-scripts to npm ci in setup action (#5062) (CP: 25.1) (#5076)

Add --ignore-scripts to npm ci in setup action (#5062)

Prevents npm postinstall scripts from executing during dependency
installation in CI workflows. This mitigates supply chain attacks
like the recent axios compromise (GHSA-fw8c-xr5c-95f9) where a
malicious postinstall script in a transitive dependency executed
arbitrary code on the runner.

Dependencies are installed from package-lock.json (npm ci), so
postinstall scripts are not needed for correct resolution. Build
steps that require compiled native modules should run npm rebuild
explicitly.

test: wait for the Kotlin Gradle application to answer before testing (#6004) (CP: 25.1) (#6008)

test: wait for the Kotlin Gradle application to answer before testing (#6004)

bootStart launched the application and then slept for ten seconds, which
is not enough on a slower machine: the Windows run had it still setting
up JPA when the integration tests connected, so all three of them failed
with "Could not connect to http://localhost:8888" and the application was
killed before it ever finished starting.

Poll the application until it serves a request instead, giving up after
two minutes. A build that starts too slowly now says so, and one whose
application dies during startup reports the exit code rather than a
connection error from every test.

test: retry the TestKit Gradle distribution download in gradle-plugin tests (#6014) (CP: 25.1) (#6019)

test: retry the TestKit Gradle distribution download in gradle-plugin tests (#6014)

The functional tests run the build under test with a pinned Gradle version,
which TestKit downloads from services.gradle.org. A network hiccup during
that download fails the test before the build even starts, which took out
four tests on the Windows runner with "Could not install Gradle distribution
from ... Unexpected end of file from server".

Retry the build up to three times when it fails while installing or
connecting to the distribution. Failures of the build under test are
rethrown as before.

* fix: work around Rolldown cross-chunk binding bug in ITs

Rolldown (used by Vite 8) has a bug where minified identifier names
in a dynamic-import chunk collide with cross-chunk runtime bindings,
causing "TypeError: t is not a function" at runtime. This affects the
markdown-helpers chunk created by @vaadin/tooltip's lazy import of
@vaadin/markdown/src/markdown-helpers.js.

to avoid the broken cross-chunk binding entirely.

Add --ignore-scripts to npm ci in setup action (#5062)

Prevents npm postinstall scripts from executing during dependency
installation in CI workflows. This mitigates supply chain attacks
like the recent axios compromise (GHSA-fw8c-xr5c-95f9) where a
malicious postinstall script in a transitive dependency executed
arbitrary code on the runner.

Dependencies are installed from package-lock.json (npm ci), so
postinstall scripts are not needed for correct resolution. Build
steps that require compiled native modules should run npm rebuild
explicitly.

chore: Make project TypeScript 6 compatible (#5209)

* fix: make custom sw.ts TS 6 compatible

Flow was upgraded to TypeScript 6, which no longer provides a global
'process' type by default. Replace 'process.env.NODE_ENV === development'
with 'import.meta.env.DEV' to match Flow's canonical sw.ts.

* fix: remove unnecessary InputEvent cast for TS 6

TS 6 infers the NumberField onInput handler parameter as InputEvent,
so the explicit 'as InputEvent' cast is flagged as unnecessary by the
no-unnecessary-type-assertion ESLint rule.

* fix: do not trigger the production frontend build from hillaGenerate

Flow 25.3 registers the production frontend bundle as an extra output
directory of the main source set (vaadin/flow#25024), which makes the
`classes` lifecycle task depend on `vaadinBuildFrontend`. Since
hillaGenerate depended on `classes`, running it started a full production
frontend build first: the bundle got built before the endpoints were
generated, and the frontend files Flow generates for the bundle -
node_modules included - were cleaned up afterwards, so the generator could
no longer resolve @vaadin/hilla-generator-cli and the task failed with

    GeneratorException: Unable to resolve npm package "@vaadin/hilla-generator-cli"

Depend on the source set compile tasks and processResources instead of the
`classes` lifecycle task, and add a functional test asserting that
hillaGenerate keeps the compile tasks but does not pull in
vaadinBuildFrontend.

test: wait for the Kotlin Gradle application to answer before testing (#6004)

bootStart launched the application and then slept for ten seconds, which
is not enough on a slower machine: the Windows run had it still setting
up JPA when the integration tests connected, so all three of them failed
with "Could not connect to http://localhost:8888" and the application was
killed before it ever finished starting.

Poll the application until it serves a request instead, giving up after
two minutes. A build that starts too slowly now says so, and one whose
application dies during startup reports the exit code rather than a
connection error from every test.

fix: keep React Fast Refresh working for views with a config export (#5576) (CP: 25.2) (#6033)

fix: keep React Fast Refresh working for views with a config export (#5576)

* fix: keep React Fast Refresh working for views with a config export

@vitejs/plugin-react v6 adds its refresh footer in a plugin that runs
after the file-router's pre-enforced transform, so the previous regex
injection into that footer never matched and editing a view with a
static `config: ViewConfig` export caused a full page reload instead of
HMR.

Replace the injection with the refresh runtime's
`window.__getReactRefreshIgnoredExports` hook: each view file registers
its module id so the `config` export is skipped during refresh boundary
validation. Config changes still propagate through the regenerated
file-routes.ts module.

Fixes #5159

* refactor: deliver the React Refresh ignore hook via a virtual module

Incorporates the improvements from #5316:

- Install window.__getReactRefreshIgnoredExports once through a virtual
  module imported by every view file, instead of duplicating the
  installer in each transformed view. View files keep registering their
  exact module ids, so private (_-prefixed) and non-route files under
  the views directory retain stock Fast Refresh semantics.
- Skip the production-mode name preservation for anonymous default
  exports, where the regex captured the function/class keyword and
  produced invalid code, and support named default class exports.
- Test the installed hook behavior (scoping, chaining with a
  pre-existing hook) in a vm context, and cover the production-mode
  transform.

test: wait for the grid rows before using them in react-crud tests (#6259)

## Summary
The `GridController` test helper handed out a grid before it had
rendered any rows, so react-crud tests failed randomly on slow CI
machines. The helper now really waits for the rows and gives a clear
error when a row is missing.

## What changed
`packages/ts/react-crud/test/GridController.ts`:

- `init()` checks now throw instead of returning a falsy value.
`waitFor` only retries when the callback throws, so the old checks
passed on the first try and returned a grid with no rows.
- `init()` also waits until `grid.loading` is `false`, because the data
provider loads items asynchronously.
- New `waitForBodyRow(row)` waits until the requested physical row
exists.
- `toggleRowSelected(row)` waits for the row before clicking it.
- `getBodyCell(row, col)` throws a named error when the row is not
rendered, instead of the confusing `Cannot read properties of undefined
(reading 'querySelectorAll')`.

## Test summary
This branch changes a shared test helper only; it adds no new test
methods.

| # | Status | What the test verifies | Why it matters |
|---|--------|------------------------|----------------|
| 1 | ✅ | Tests that call `GridController.init()` and then read rows or
toggle selection (the existing react-crud grid, AutoGrid and AutoCrud
suites) now run against a grid that has finished loading | This was the
actual flake: without the wait, row lookups returned `undefined` on slow
machines |
| 2 | ❗ **gap** | `waitForBodyRow` / `getBodyCell` throw a descriptive
error when a row never renders | If this regressed, real failures would
again show up as an unrelated `querySelectorAll` error and be hard to
debug |

- No test method was added or changed. Row 1 is covered indirectly by
every existing react-crud test that uses `GridController`.

Deliberately untested: the helper's own error messages (row 2). They
only improve failure output, and adding a test for a test helper's error
text was not judged worth the extra fixture.
